title: One performance. Two characters.
summary: Riko and Nami share one recorded performance. Independently reviewed character clips become a four-second vertical identity cut through free local composition.

inputs.label: Riko identity plate
inputs.description: An FX-owned canonical illustration fitted onto a portrait plate without repainting. The complete source illustration is included separately.

inputs.label: Nami identity plate
inputs.description: The same Nami concept used in other FX examples, fitted with extra room for the long rabbit ears.

inputs.label: Pinned driving performance
inputs.description: A four-second interval from Polina Tankilevitch on Pexels, explicitly prepared at 24fps. Acquire the source from its publisher; raw and trimmed stock footage is excluded from FX delivery.

stages.label: Prepare the exact references
stages.description: Free preparation crops transparent margins, fits existing character pixels, removes source audio, and converts the selected interval to 24fps without temporal interpolation.

stages.label: Transfer and independently review Riko
stages.description: One motion call preserves the character identity while following the real performance; a different model checks the identity and eight synchronized driving/result pairs.

stages.label: Reuse the utility for Nami
stages.description: The same workflow and motion reference use a different identity plate. A clipped-ear candidate was rejected; the selected candidate uses a smaller starting plate.

stages.label: Cut between identities on one shared timeline
stages.description: The cast graph reuses the accepted paid results. A caller-selected common region contains all recorded native-frame foreground bounds and keeps the fitted stage fixed. Riko supplies seconds 0–2 and Nami seconds 2–4 from the same driving timeline. Local composition adds typography, converts to 30fps without interpolation and decodes all 120 frames. The 3.2-second poster and identity-cut boundary received separate full-resolution review.

outputs.label: Shared-timeline intervals, lineage and poster timestamp
Dense samples across the two-second identity cut

Full-resolution frame immediately after the identity cut

stages.label: Compare both complete performances
stages.description: The alternate eight-second sequence shows the full four-second Riko take followed by the full four-second Nami take. Its video is unchanged from the earlier accepted composition; the upright Riko poster is selected at 3.2 seconds. Historical review names are rebound to the exact retained assets, with original review bytes preserved as snapshots.

outputs.label: Original sequence verdict with retained asset bindings

stages.label: Try a different lower-body performance
stages.description: An additional six-second Riko take follows a different reference with one-leg balance and leg extension. Independent review covers 24 paired poses, five native-resolution comparisons and the poster. Relaxed source hands become splayed or V-like fingers, and the plain studio background does not establish exact floor contact or physical balance. Source provenance and acquisition instructions accompany the paired evidence; raw and transcoded stock footage are excluded.

limitations: The character utility is a bounded performance-transfer stage. The reel is an example composition; larger stories, copy, music, voiceover and platform delivery belong to the caller.

The studio-border proxy checks all native frames for edge contact; it does not establish semantic quality. Independent character review covers the identity and eight synchronized pose samples. It cannot certify every transition, fine fingers, continuous foot contact or reliability on unseen inputs.

The primary is an editorial cut between two identities on one driving timeline, not a seamless morph or loop. Nami appears shorter and lower in the stage than Riko; the exact cut and common framing were reviewed for these accepted clips and must be checked again on fresh takes.

Native character clips are 720x1280 at 24fps. Caller-selected fixed regions remove empty background before local composition into 1080x1920 at 30fps by frame duplication; no intermediate motion is generated. Output is silent.

The selected driving footage is used as an adaptation under the recorded licensing interpretation, not as a training dataset. Raw and trimmed stock footage is acquired from its publisher and is not hosted by FX.
Riko and Nami are the public cast. A third local development character is excluded because upstream reference rights remain unresolved.

The additional lower-body study broadens the inspected inputs without establishing a success rate. Its relaxed source hand poses become splayed or V-like fingers; exact floor contact, physical balance and every transition are outside its bounded review.
